name: Stamm 1980
question: Does daily low-dose antimicrobial prophylaxis prevent recurrent urinary tract infection in women compared with placebo?

design.population: 60 women with recurrent urinary tract infections.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, title and Results; PubMed publication type: Randomized Controlled Trial

verdictNote: All three antibiotics lowered infection incidence during the six-month treatment period.
takeaway: Daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, or nitrofurantoin macrocrystals each reduced recurrent urinary tract infections versus placebo during six months of prophylaxis; the protective effect ended after treatment stopped.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print gives June 1980; day 1 is imputed
reports.citation: Stamm WE, Counts GW, Wagner KF, et al. "Antimicrobial prophylaxis of recurrent urinary tract infections: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Ann Intern Med.* 1980;92(6):770-775. doi:10.7326/0003-4819-92-6-770
reports.followUp: Six months of prophylaxis; post-treatment follow-up duration not stated in the abstract.

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis
results.note: Placebo versus this drug regimen; arm sizes and infection counts are not stated in the abstract.

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of trimethoprim prophylaxis
results.note: Placebo versus this drug regimen; arm sizes and infection counts are not stated in the abstract.

results.measure: Infections per patient-year during six months of nitrofurantoin prophylaxis
results.note: Placebo versus this drug regimen; arm sizes and infection counts are not stated in the abstract.

results.measure: Recurrence in women with at least three infections in the year before prophylaxis
results.note: Infections were more likely after prophylaxis in women with at least three preprophylaxis infections per year; no group counts reported.

harms.label: Post-prophylaxis non-E. coli infections and resistance
harms.note: Non-E. coli infections occurred more often after prophylaxis (P < 0.05); emergence of trimethoprim-resistant E. coli was described as rare, without counts.

delivery.label: Once-daily prophylactic regimens
delivery.value: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 40 mg/200 mg, trimethoprim 100 mg, nitrofurantoin macrocrystals 100 mg, or placebo for six months.
